report.summary: Chunk 2 of bus.py: defines constants, regex patterns, hashing functions, identity/path helpers, and a cache. Claims about non-body fields, allowed keys, and path resolution are partially checkable.
risks: _APPEND_CACHE | medium | Global mutable cache keyed by resolved path, invalidated by (size, mtime_ns). Race conditions possible if multiple threads write to same file; no lock shown for cache access. | Check if cache access is protected by _WRITE_LOCK or another mechanism.

_resolve_store | medium | Mentions refusing paths under '<repo>/memory/' but code is truncated; the check may be missing or incomplete. | Inspect the rest of _resolve_store to confirm the memory-path check is implemented.

claims.text: fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: The claim about growth complexity and per-council budget refers to session.py and to transcript behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor: 'claude said X' is not reproducible six months out, because the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it.
claims.why: The claim refers to ADR-010 and reproducibility concerns not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: The claim about rejection behavior is not implemented in this chunk; no validation logic is shown.

claims.text: Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns). Re-parsing the whole transcript per append is O(n^2) overall; a 500-turn council must not pay that.
claims.why: The cache invalidation and usage logic is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: The content projection body_sha is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: canonical_body filters out keys in _NON_BODY_FIELDS, which are 'ts', 'prev', 'entry_sha', 'id', 'body_sha' as defined above.

claims.text: The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: Function returns json.dumps of canonical_body with sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True, producing deterministic bytes.

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal unknown by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: The claim about caller behavior is not verifiable from this function; actor_id just formats the string.

claims.text: One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing 'the file' may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: evidence_ref returns dict with path (normalized forward slashes) and sha256 of the provided data bytes.

claims.text: <base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl. council_id is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: council_store_path calls _check_council_id which validates against _COUNCIL_ID_RE; no sanitization is performed, so a rewritten id would be a different council_id.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: The claim about chain walk and truncation detection is not verifiable from this function alone; it only returns the path.

claims.text: Resolve and REFUSE any path under <repo>/memory/. Council turns must never reach the memory ledger (see module docstring).
claims.why: The function body is truncated; the check for memory path is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: Constants for allowed keys are defined but no validation logic is present in this chunk.
Global cache _APPEND_CACHE is mutable and unprotected; potential race condition if multiple threads append concurrently.
_resolve_store is truncated; the memory-path rejection claim cannot be verified.
Regex _ACTOR_RE allows a broad pattern including colons and plus signs; may be more permissive than intended.
